title: Shift in equilibrium: Fe3+ and SCN-
objective: Observe the intense red colour of the [FeSCN]2+ complex ion
Predict and observe the effect of adding more Fe3+ or SCN- on the colour intensity
Predict and observe the effect of removing Fe3+ (by adding a complexing agent) on the colour
Explain each observation using Le Chatelier's principle and the reaction quotient Q

theory.statement: Fe3+(aq, pale yellow) and SCN-(aq, colourless) exist in equilibrium with the intensely blood-red complex ion [FeSCN]2+(aq): Fe3+ + SCN- ⇌ [FeSCN]2+. Because the product is so strongly coloured while the reactants are almost colourless, the depth of colour is a direct, visual proxy for how far the equilibrium lies to the right.
theory.derivationNote: By Le Chatelier's principle, increasing the concentration of either reactant (Fe3+ or SCN-) shifts the equilibrium to the right, deepening the red colour. Adding a reagent that removes Fe3+ from solution — such as sodium oxalate, which forms the stable, colourless [Fe(C2O4)3]3- complex — lowers the free Fe3+ concentration and shifts the equilibrium to the LEFT, fading the colour, even though nothing was added or removed from the SCN- side directly.
keyEquations: Le Chatelier: a stress that increases a reactant shifts equilibrium towards products, and vice versa

apparatus.name: Sodium oxalate solution
apparatus.why: Removes free Fe3+ by forming a stable, colourless oxalato complex

apparatus.name: Test tubes and test tube stand
apparatus.why: Holds separate portions of the equilibrium mixture for comparison

apparatus.name: White tile or white background
apparatus.why: Makes small differences in colour intensity easier to judge

procedure.text: Mix dilute FeCl3 and KSCN solutions to give a pale red-orange reference mixture; divide it into four test tubes.
To the first tube add a little more FeCl3 solution and compare the colour with the reference.
To the second tube add a little more KSCN solution and compare.
To the third tube add sodium oxalate solution drop by drop and watch the colour fade.
To the fourth tube add water and compare (dilution alone).
Explain each colour change in terms of the equilibrium shifting left or right.

steps: Add each reagent to a separate portion of the equilibrium mixture
Observe and record the colour change
State whether the equilibrium shifted towards products or reactants

expectedResult.quantity: Direction of the equilibrium shift on adding excess Fe3+ or SCN-
expectedResult.statement: Adding extra FeCl3 or KSCN deepens the red colour (equilibrium shifts right, towards [FeSCN]2+). Adding sodium oxalate removes free Fe3+ and fades the colour (equilibrium shifts left) — demonstrating that a stress need not add or remove a species written explicitly in the equilibrium to shift it; removing Fe3+ indirectly has the same effect as removing it directly.

safety: FeCl3 solution can stain skin and clothing; handle over a tray.
KSCN is toxic if ingested — do not pipette by mouth.
Dispose of thiocyanate-containing waste as directed, not down the sink in quantity.
sourcesOfError: Judging colour intensity by eye is subjective; use a consistent white background and viewing angle.
Using too concentrated a reagent makes the colour so dark that further shifts are hard to see.
Old or diluted stock solutions give weaker colours unrelated to the equilibrium itself.

viva.question: Why does adding sodium oxalate fade the red colour, even though oxalate does not appear in the Fe3+/SCN- equilibrium?
viva.expectedConcept: Oxalate ions form a stable, colourless complex with free Fe3+, lowering its concentration in solution. By Le Chatelier's principle, removing a reactant (Fe3+) shifts the equilibrium Fe3+ + SCN- ⇌ [FeSCN]2+ to the LEFT, so some of the red complex dissociates and the colour fades.
viva.answerLogic: An indirect removal of a reactant via a side equilibrium.
viva.commonMisconception: Thinking oxalate must react directly with SCN- or with the complex itself.

viva.question: What would you expect if you added a large excess of both FeCl3 and KSCN together?
viva.expectedConcept: The colour would deepen even further than adding either alone, since both reactant concentrations rise together, pushing the equilibrium further to the right.
viva.answerLogic: Combined effect of two reactant increases.

viva.question: Why is this particular equilibrium ([FeSCN]2+) so well suited to demonstrating Le Chatelier's principle visually?
viva.expectedConcept: Because the product is intensely coloured while both reactants are nearly colourless, so the position of equilibrium can be read directly from colour intensity without any instrument.
viva.answerLogic: A strong, exclusive colour signal from one species.
viva.commonMisconception: Thinking any equilibrium could be observed this easily.

preLab.question: Adding more KSCN to the Fe3+/SCN- equilibrium mixture will:
preLab.feedback: Adding a reactant shifts the equilibrium towards the product, deepening the red [FeSCN]2+ colour.

duringLab.question: Test at least four different reagents/conditions.

postLab.question: Sodium oxalate fades the red colour because it:
options: Removes free Fe3+ as a stable complex
Is itself red and masks the colour
postLab.feedback: Oxalate complexes Fe3+, lowering its free concentration and shifting the equilibrium left.

assumptions: Reaction reaches equilibrium quickly enough to observe as a steady colour
The complexing side-reaction (oxalate) goes essentially to completion
edgeCases: High reagent concentration saturates the colour change
expectedBehaviour: Colour deepens on adding a reactant, fades on removing one
